notes:
Own chips compiled into one function each, inside shown live

A RISC-V datapath is mostly own chips; worked out part by part each
change costs a call per gate. A chip is now compiled once into Python:
its gates as expressions in order from the inputs, parts with memory
called on copies of their prims (one set per chip on the board), and
another round only while those change or a gate feeds back. A 32-bit
adder as one chip runs three times as fast as opened up; a small
computer whose half-clocks change little gets a bit slower but still
does 13,000 clocks a second. A chip with two outputs on one net is
opened up as before so the conflict stays visible.

Double-clicking a compiled chip now shows the values of that very chip
on the board, with its memory, while time runs on.
